title: Recoverability and Verifier Strength: Two Measured Preconditions for Unattended Agent Self-Improvement
abstract: arXiv:2610.27465v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent platforms are starting to improve their own agents: they read a deployed agent's execution traces, derive a change, have an automated verifier approve it, and release it with no human author. How much of this loop can safely run without a human? We propose two quantities a platform can measure. Verifier strength $\sigma$ is how well the available verifier -- often an LLM judge -- agrees with a trusted reference verifier; it limits how much a step can improve the agent. Recoverability is how cheaply a bad change can be undone: whether undoing it needs a new verifier approval, and how much of the old behavior a rollback restores. A step should run unattended only if both are adequate. On our platform this rule allows prompt, tool and skill edits to run unattended and keeps weight updates under human sign-off.   Our main contribution is these two definitions and how to measure them. We built a platform that applies the rule and tested

translated_title: 可恢复性与验证器强度：无人值守智能体自我改进的两个可测量前置条件
translated_abstract: 智能体平台开始改进自身的智能体：它们读取已部署智能体的执行轨迹，推导出变更，让自动化验证器批准该变更，并在没有人类作者的情况下发布。这个循环中有多少可以安全地在无人参与的情况下运行？我们提出了平台可以测量的两个量。验证器强度 σ 衡量可用验证器（通常是 LLM 判官）与可信参考验证器的一致程度，它限制了一个步骤能在多大程度上改进智能体。可恢复性衡量撤销一个不良变更的代价有多低：撤销它是否需要新的验证器批准，以及回滚能恢复多少旧行为。只有当两者都充分时，一个步骤才应该无人值守运行。在我们的平台上，这一规则允许提示词、工具和技能编辑无人值守运行，同时使权重更新保持在人类签署批准之下。我们的主要贡献是这两个定义及其测量方法。我们构建了一个应用该规则的平台并进行了测试。
tldr: 论文提出了“验证器强度”和“可恢复性”这两个可测量的前置条件，用于判断智能体平台的哪些自我改进步骤可以安全地无人值守运行。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes two measurable preconditions—verifier strength and recoverability—for agent platforms to determine which self-improvement steps can safely run without human supervision.
